I've worked this land for 20 years. I don't need a book to tell me what to do — I know this soil, I know this weather, I know what the markets want. Quzhou gets dry spells in spring so the well pump matters. My family is four people and 349.9 mu is a lot of land to manage, so I have to keep things simple and do what I know works.

Sweetpotato is my main business — the sandy loam here suits it, the starch buyers come every autumn, and I know how to ridge and store. I'll put most of my land into that. Maize I keep because my household eats it and the summer rains help fill it out without too much pump cost. Millet I throw onto my poorer, drier plots — it survives on little water and I can sell it locally. No point trying new varieties I don't know. I'll use what I've used before.

I plough deep for sweetpotato to get good roots. Maize I just rotary-till to save time. Millet the same. I fertilize by feel and what my neighbors do — a bit more potassium on the sweetpotato because that's what makes the roots swell. I water when the plants look stressed, not on a fixed schedule. Pesticides when I see bugs or spots, not before.
